items.claim: ERD entity fields had name and type swapped against the ER reader/writer, so PK/FK were lost on export
The UML interface's `«interface»` was exported as the class name, with the real name written as an attribute
The UML abstract class marked abstractness only with italics, which the class writer drops
items.note: It now has a `<<abstract>>` row and the method is written `+ draw()*`. The stencil grew to 124 tall for the extra row.

items.claim: The mind-map subtopic's `stadium` has no Mermaid mind-map bracket
items.note: The subtopic is now `rect`. `floating-note`'s `note` outline: not a defect, because a floating note is a separate root, which the mind-map writer drops whatever its outline.

items.claim: The BPMN end event differed from a start event only by stroke width, so draw.io wrote it as a start event and read draw.io's own end event back as a start event
items.note: It now has its own `endEvent` outline, a circle with a filled heavy ring. draw.io maps it to `outline=end` both ways, and Mermaid writes it as the nearest circle. `figureOver` now passes an outline's `solid` part through. This adds an outline name, so its changeset is `minor`.

items.claim: `expectStencilsBuild` counted only label and field rows, though `stencilInsertOps` also makes nodes for header rows and their asides
`expectStencilsBuild` left the `console.warn` spy in place when an assertion failed

items.note: without a failing test. The body grows to fit its rows as measured in their own style, so no stencil can lay out a row narrower than its styled text. Now the check at least measures what it says it does.

items.claim: The test helper `authoredScene` placed stencils in `DEFAULT_NODE_STYLE` instead of the theme's role style, as the real stencil tool does. Every authored mind map therefore warned "hold no colors" on export
items.note: which also makes `mermaidRoundTrip` return the writer's warnings. It is test-only, so it has no changeset.
